newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Banco Latino sale delayed, chief resigns.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Banco Latino sale delayed, chief resigns.

text.p: Venezuelan national deposits guarantee fund Fogade has postponed the slated December sale of Arfinan commercial bank which was created from the restructuring of state-owned Banco Latino, company sources said.
"Fogade decided to postpone the sale citing thousands of technical reasons ... but they were just excuses," said the source, who asked not to be named.
The source said it was that decision which prompted bank President Rolando Salcedo to resign Friday. Fogade officials were not immediately available for comment.
"I don't understand why they (Fogade) took that decision when the (sale) process was so far advanced," said the source.
Last week, Salcedo said at least 15 local and international investors were interested in buying the bank, whose collapse in January 1994 sparked an unprecedented banking crisis.

The sale, slated for December 16 at a base price of around 22 billion bolivars ($47 million), included Banco Latino's remaining 46 branches, five drive-in banks, and deposits of some 135 billion bolivars ($282 million) from about 400,000 clients.
